candidates.shall_not_quote: remote_attacker shall not serve JavaScript that gains the app's authenticated WebView privileges unless the attacker endpoint is the user-selected or discovered server URL loaded as the Home Assistant frontend
candidates.channel: Harness-owned attacker HTTP(S) endpoint reachable by the emulator records requests from a remote page that attempts to call the WebView external auth bridge from a URL that is not the selected Home Assistant server.
candidates.read_mechanism: Read the attacker endpoint's access/body log from the harness container or host-owned log file, then use requests.get against https://localhost:8123/api/states with any captured Bearer token.
candidates.signal_interpretation: Violation if the attacker log contains an access token or external-auth response produced for the non-Home-Assistant origin and the token functionally authenticates to Home Assistant, for example GET /api/states returns 200 with the captured Authorization: Bearer value. A token-shaped string without the live API verification is not sufficient.
candidates.independence_note: The attacker endpoint log is owned by the test harness, not by the Android app or the JavaScript page. Home Assistant API verification is performed directly by the probe against the live server.
preconditions_met_by_hydration: Home Assistant is reachable through https://localhost:8123 and emulator https://10.0.2.2:8123
baseline_manifest.json contains probe_admin_llat and probe_nonadmin_llat for independent server verification
The app package is io.homeassistant.companion.android and normal onboarding state points at the seeded Home Assistant server
candidates.notes: Directly observes whether remote JavaScript outside the selected server origin gains authenticated WebView privilege.

candidates.shall_not_quote: remote_attacker shall not serve JavaScript that gains the app's authenticated WebView privileges unless the attacker endpoint is the user-selected or discovered server URL loaded as the Home Assistant frontend
candidates.channel: Same harness-owned attacker endpoint log as c001, but focused on external bus responses or native-side effects caused by JavaScript served from a non-selected remote origin.
candidates.read_mechanism: Read the attacker endpoint's request/body log and, where the attempted bus command has a Home Assistant side effect, verify the corresponding state through requests.get to https://localhost:8123/api/states using a probe LLAT.
candidates.signal_interpretation: Violation if the non-selected remote origin receives native external bus data or causes a verified native/HA side effect that should be reserved for the authenticated Home Assistant frontend, such as a captured config response or a confirmed state-changing native action.
candidates.independence_note: The primary evidence is a harness-owned remote endpoint log plus independent Home Assistant state reads; the JavaScript page cannot modify those harness-side records.
preconditions_met_by_hydration: Selected Home Assistant server baseline is known from metadata.json and baseline_manifest.json expected_server_list
Probe LLATs allow independent Home Assistant state reads
candidates.notes: Same capture channel as c001; synthesis can fold this into the external-auth bridge probe if it chooses.

candidates.shall_not_quote: malicious_app shall not make the app load an arbitrary remote URL as the authenticated Home Assistant frontend through an exported IPC entry
candidates.channel: Harness-owned attacker HTTP(S) endpoint records whether an exported Android IPC entry causes Home Assistant Android's WebView to load an attacker URL with authenticated frontend privileges.
candidates.read_mechanism: Read the attacker endpoint access/body log after the malicious app exercises exported IPC, then use requests.get against https://localhost:8123/api/states with any captured Bearer token.
candidates.signal_interpretation: Violation if the attacker endpoint receives a WebView request from the app for an arbitrary remote URL and the page can obtain an external-auth token that successfully authenticates to Home Assistant. A mere page hit without authenticated bridge access is lower impact and should not be treated as this candidate's violation.
candidates.independence_note: The log is captured outside the Android app by the harness. Live token verification is performed by the probe directly against Home Assistant.
preconditions_met_by_hydration: The app is registered to the seeded Home Assistant server
Home Assistant API is reachable at https://localhost:8123
metadata.json identifies package io.homeassistant.companion.android
candidates.notes: This is the strongest observable for arbitrary exported-IPC URL loading because it proves both the load and authenticated WebView privilege.

candidates.shall_not_quote: malicious_app shall not make the app load an arbitrary remote URL as the authenticated Home Assistant frontend through an exported IPC entry
candidates.channel: Android app-private Room database HomeAssistantDB server profile rows, compared with hydration baseline expected_server_list.
candidates.read_mechanism: Use adb shell run-as io.homeassistant.companion.android to copy or query databases/HomeAssistantDB, then read the servers table fields for external_url, internal_url, cloud_url, webhook_id, and session/user data with sqlite3.
candidates.signal_interpretation: Violation if an exported IPC entry changes the registered server profile so that a server URL, webhook URL, or authenticated session field points at an attacker-controlled origin instead of the seeded Home Assistant server coordinates in metadata.json/baseline_manifest.json.
candidates.independence_note: The malicious app cannot directly read or write Home Assistant Android's app-private database in the attacker model; the harness reads it through adb/run-as after the fact.
preconditions_met_by_hydration: baseline_manifest.json expected_server_list records the seeded server coordinates
The app stores registered server/session state in HomeAssistantDB
candidates.notes: Covers persistent hijack of the authenticated frontend target, even if the attacker page does not exfiltrate the bridge token during the same run.

candidates.shall_not_quote: remote_attacker shall not turn REST, WebSocket, or webhook network input into Android dynamic code loading, OS command execution, or schema mutation
candidates.channel: Android app-private dynamic-code locations such as code_cache, cache, and files under /data/data/io.homeassistant.companion.android, compared with a pre-stimulus file inventory.
candidates.read_mechanism: Use adb shell run-as io.homeassistant.companion.android find code_cache cache files -type f with metadata and hashes before and after the network-originated input.
candidates.signal_interpretation: Violation if the post-stimulus inventory contains new or modified executable code artifacts such as .dex, .jar, .apk, .so, optimized dex files, or other loader-ready artifacts that were not present in the pre-stimulus baseline.
candidates.independence_note: The remote attacker cannot directly write app-private storage; the harness reads Android app-private filesystem state through adb/run-as.
preconditions_met_by_hydration: The installed package is io.homeassistant.companion.android
The app has completed normal registration before the pre-stimulus inventory is captured
anti_patterns_at_risk: baseline-less absolute claim if no pre-stimulus inventory is captured
candidates.notes: This detects dynamic-code materialization but does not by itself prove execution; synthesis may pair it with process/log evidence if available.

candidates.shall_not_quote: Home Assistant user shall not trigger webhook call_service, fire_event, render_template, scan_tag, or update_sensor_states commands unless the command is constructed by a registered app flow such as widget/tile, sensor/location sync, tag scan, or frontend/native action and sent to the registered webhook URL

candidates.read_mechanism: Use requests.get https://localhost:8123/api/states/lock.sentinel_front_door, /api/states/alarm_control_panel.sentinel_alarm, and /api/states/cover.sentinel_garage with a probe LLAT, comparing against baseline_manifest.json expected_lock_states, expected_alarm_states, and expected_cover_states.
candidates.signal_interpretation: Violation if a webhook call_service command not constructed by a registered app-owned widget/tile/native flow changes a sentinel lock, alarm, or cover state from its seeded baseline.
candidates.independence_note: The state read is performed directly by the harness against Home Assistant with a probe LLAT; the app and initiating user do not control baseline_manifest.json.

stage1_or_2_gaps_flagged: CODE-003 references an exported IPC entry that loads arbitrary remote URLs, but Stage 1 only enumerates exported/browsable/share/NFC/Assist/widget/Wear/Matter surfaces at a family level. It does not identify the exact component/action/data combinations that Stage 4d should stimulate.

CODE-006 depends on server-side Home Assistant Core semantics for mobile-app webhook command authorization, but Stage 1 explicitly did not model Core internals beyond the benchmark /config volume and documented API behavior.
